questions.subject: Flask
questions.question: Explain the difference between URL variable rules and url_for in Flask.
questions.ideal_answer: URL variable rules and url_for differ in several ways: URL variable rules is dynamic route segments (works by type conversion and validation) whereas url_for is URL generation (works by reverse routing). URL variable rules is typically used for <converter:variable_name>, while url_for is used for endpoint name, argument binding. Example demonstrating URL variable rules: @app.route('/user/<int:user_id>'). Example demonstrating url_for: url_for('user_profile', user_id=1).

questions.question: Explain the difference between request context and app factory pattern in Flask.
questions.ideal_answer:
request context and app factory pattern differ in several ways: request context is request-level state (works by per-request data isolation) whereas app factory pattern is application creation function (works by testability and configuration flexibility). request context is typically used for request, session objects, while app factory pattern is used for create_app(config_name). def index(): return request.method. Example demonstrating app factory pattern: def create_app(config_name='default'): app = Flask(__name__); app.config.from_object(configs[config_name]); return app.
